name: Nirvana
label: Sub Pop
lede: Three kids from logging country, a $606.17 debut, one record that knocked Michael Jackson off the top of the chart, and a story that ended in a Seattle greenhouse seven years after it started.

eras.title: Aberdeen, a borrowed drummer, and a string of bad names
eras.text: Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic met through the Melvins crowd in Aberdeen, Washington, a mill town two hours from Seattle. For a year the band had no fixed name and no fixed drummer, and it was a producer's tape, not a gig, that got them noticed.

years.cap: Casting call for the Smells Like Teen Spirit video, 1991 · Wikimedia
yt: Full audio of the Raymond house party, March 1987
years.h: First show: a house party at 17 Nussbaum Road, Raymond
years.p: Kurt Cobain, Krist Novoselic and drummer [[Aaron Burckhard|86d3f2c7-2a19-4249-ad7c-6feec74118d7]] play a keg party in Raymond, Washington, to a room of locals who mostly want classic rock. Someone taped it.
years.xp:
The Raymond set mixed early originals with a cover of [[Flipper|4e99b3a5-654b-43ee-a9bf-c55c155c0495]]'s Sex Bomb. Novoselic hung off furniture; the partygoers, by most accounts, didn't know what to make of it.

Through 1987 the trio played as Skid Row, Pen Cap Chew, Bliss and Ted Ed Fred before settling on a name. Burckhard was gone by the end of the year.

years.h: A Jack Endino demo tape with Melvins drummer Dale Crover
years.p: With [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] drummer [[Dale Crover|9b93a71b-1484-4bea-b096-f660c1161f8a]] sitting in, Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic cut ten songs in one day at [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]]'s Reciprocal Recording. Endino passes the tape to Sub Pop's Jonathan Poneman.

years.h: First show as Nirvana: Community World Theater, Tacoma
years.p: After a year of throwaway names, the band plays Tacoma's Community World Theater billed as Nirvana for the first time.

years.h: Chad Channing takes over the drum stool
years.p: [[Chad Channing|e2f28104-72bb-4c8f-b0f9-78d4eaf492fd]], a drummer from Bainbridge Island, plays his first Nirvana show and becomes the band's first long-term drummer.

years.h: Love Buzz: Sub Pop Singles Club No. 1, 1,000 copies
years.p: Nirvana's first single is a cover of Shocking Blue's Love Buzz, sold by mail to Sub Pop's new Singles Club subscribers in a hand-numbered run of 1,000.

eras.title: A $606.17 album and a revolving drum stool
eras.text: Bleach made Nirvana one of Sub Pop's working bands and sent them to Europe in a cramped van with Tad. By the end of 1990 they had tapes with Butch Vig, a new drummer from Washington, D.C., and major labels calling.

years.h: Bleach: recorded with Jack Endino for $606.17
years.p: Nirvana's debut, made at Reciprocal Recording between Christmas Eve 1988 and January 24, 1989. Kurt Cobain's pop song About a Girl sits among the sludge.
years.xp: The studio bill of $606.17 was covered by [[Jason Everman|797dc323-fc39-4597-98cc-d10493f67326]], a guitarist who joined just after the sessions and was credited on the sleeve without playing a note. According to Wikipedia, Bleach sold about 40,000 copies in its first run.

years.h: Jason Everman leaves after one American tour
years.p: Jason Everman is out after Nirvana's first U.S. tour. Everman has said he quit; Kurt Cobain said the band fired him. Within months he is playing bass in [[Soundgarden|153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4]].
years.xp: Everman lasted about a year in Soundgarden before being fired in 1990. He later joined the U.S. Army, served as a Ranger and in Special Forces, and studied at Columbia University.

years.h: Kurt Cobain climbs a speaker stack in Rome
years.p: Worn down on a European tour with [[Tad|867d3fb7-9cd1-47a4-a8f0-de29cdca2004]], Kurt Cobain climbs the PA at a Rome show mid-set and threatens to jump, as told in Michael Azerrad's Come as You Are.

years.h: Butch Vig sessions at Smart Studios, Madison
years.p: Nirvana record songs for a second Sub Pop album with [[Butch Vig|ba30915c-4d33-43c5-8c37-ead0b8061517]] in Madison, Wisconsin. The tapes circulate among major labels and do more for the band than any release.

years.h: Chad Channing leaves Nirvana
years.p: Chad Channing departs, frustrated at having little say in the songwriting. Nirvana go looking for a harder-hitting drummer.

years.h: Sliver: cut in an hour with Mudhoney's Dan Peters
years.p: Recorded July 11 at Reciprocal during a break in a [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]] session, with [[Dan Peters|3402566b-20dc-47f1-973b-2af1dedae702]] drumming. It is Nirvana's last new release on Sub Pop.

years.h: Dave Grohl flies in from Scream's collapse
years.p: When D.C. punk band [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]] fell apart in Los Angeles, [[Buzz Osborne|9a911b22-f972-44ee-b2d3-d41297fe96e9]] put drummer [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]] in touch with Nirvana. Grohl flew to Seattle, auditioned, and was in.
years.xp: Grohl was in the crowd on September 22 at the Motor Sports International Garage in Seattle for the one show Dan Peters played with Nirvana. He had joined Scream at 17 and toured Europe and the U.S. with them before the band stranded in L.A. when its bassist left.

years.h: Dave Grohl's first Nirvana show: North Shore Surf Club, Olympia
years.p: Dave Grohl plays his first show with Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic at the North Shore Surf Club in Olympia.

eras.title: Number one by accident
eras.text: Nirvana signed to Sonic Youth's label on Kim Gordon's recommendation, expecting modest sales. Nevermind instead sold hundreds of thousands a week, pulled Sub Pop out of debt, and put three men who'd been sleeping in vans on the cover of every magazine.

years.h: Nirvana sign to DGC; Sub Pop gets $75,000 and a cut
years.p: Nirvana sign to Geffen's DGC for a $287,000 advance over two albums. To release them, Sub Pop takes $75,000 and two percent of the next two records.
years.xp: Those points on Nevermind and Incesticide became a financial lifeline for Sub Pop, which had been close to broke in 1991.

years.h: Where the title Smells Like Teen Spirit came from
years.p: [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] of [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]] wrote on Kurt Cobain's wall that he smelled like Teen Spirit. Teen Spirit was the deodorant his girlfriend [[Tobi Vail|0a5c5a29-5bcd-4a8b-9ec0-b0c4d2e28851]] wore; Kurt Cobain didn't know, and heard it as a slogan.

years.h: Nevermind: DGC hoped for 250,000 copies
years.p: The baby on the cover is four-month-old Spencer Elden, shot underwater by Kirk Weddle. By December, Nevermind was selling about 400,000 copies a week in the U.S., according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: Butch Vig produced at Sound City in Van Nuys that May, and [[Andy Wallace|665695c1-d546-4141-8dd7-1cd40a1eea71]] mixed. Kurt Cobain later said the glossy finish embarrassed him.

years.cap: A guitar Kurt Cobain smashed, MoPOP · Wikimedia
years.h: Nevermind knocks Michael Jackson from No. 1, same day as SNL
years.p: Nevermind displaces Michael Jackson's Dangerous at the top of the Billboard 200 the same day Nirvana play Saturday Night Live. They end the broadcast with Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic kissing.

years.h: Kurt Cobain marries Courtney Love on a Waikiki beach
years.p: Kurt Cobain marries [[Hole|1dcc8968-f2cd-441c-beda-6270f70f2863]] singer [[Courtney Love|31d2041c-985d-48f7-b6e2-2a70cdf14853]] in Honolulu. Their daughter Frances Bean Cobain is born that August 18.

years.h: Kurt Cobain's retroactive publishing demand nearly splits Nirvana
years.p: Kurt Cobain demands most of the songwriting royalties, backdated to Nevermind. Krist Novoselic and Dave Grohl agree, and the band survives.
years.xp: Under the settlement Novoselic and Grohl shared in only eleven songs, with 12.5 percent each on Smells Like Teen Spirit; Cobain took the rest. The deal left them dependent on record, tour and merchandise income while Cobain held most of the publishing.

years.cap: Kurt Cobain's house in Seattle · Wikimedia
years.h: Reading 1992: Kurt Cobain arrives in a wheelchair
years.p: Headlining the last night of Reading, Kurt Cobain is wheeled onstage in a hospital gown and wig by writer [[Everett True|001897b1-fbb7-4dbe-b1df-ac638bf60afc]], mocking the rumors about his health, then stands up and plays.

years.h: MTV VMAs: Nirvana start Rape Me, then play Lithium
years.p: MTV refused to let Nirvana play Rape Me. They tease its opening anyway, switch to Lithium, and Krist Novoselic throws his bass into the air and it lands on his head.

years.h: Incesticide: DGC and Sub Pop split the rarities
years.p: B-sides, BBC sessions and the Dale Crover demo, released jointly by DGC and Sub Pop to beat the bootleggers. Kurt Cobain painted the cover.

eras.title: Steve Albini, a silent audience, and the end
eras.text: Nirvana answered Nevermind with a record meant to scare off casual fans and a stripped-down TV set that became their best-loved live document. Five months after the Unplugged taping, Kurt Cobain was dead.

years.h: Puss / Oh, the Guilt: a split with the Jesus Lizard
years.p: Nirvana share a Touch and Go single with [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]], a nod to the Chicago noise rock Kurt Cobain loved.

years.h: Steve Albini records In Utero; the label wants it softer
years.p: [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] recorded In Utero in about two weeks at Pachyderm Studio in Cannon Falls, Minnesota. When press reports said the label hated it, Heart-Shaped Box and All Apologies were remixed by Scott Litt.
years.xp:
Albini took a flat fee and no royalties, saying it would be unethical to take points. The sessions cost about $25,000, according to Wikipedia.

In April 1993 the Chicago Tribune's Greg Kot reported that Geffen found the album unreleasable; the band publicly denied label pressure, but the two singles were remixed before release.

years.h: In Utero debuts at No. 1, and Walmart gets a different cover
years.p: For Walmart and Kmart, Nirvana altered the back-cover collage and listed Rape Me as Waif Me.

years.h: Pat Smear of the Germs joins as a second guitarist
years.p: [[Pat Smear|3da65013-dfdd-40c7-b9c7-e4c829862c66]], guitarist in L.A. punk band [[Germs|42c4b58d-2e28-41d4-bfe5-4edee68386cf]], joins for the In Utero tour, the second guitarist Nirvana had tried to find since Jason Everman.

years.h: MTV Unplugged: lilies, candles, and hardly any hits
years.p: Nirvana tape MTV Unplugged at Sony Music Studios with cellist Lori Goldston and [[Meat Puppets|3df040ee-2b8b-446b-937a-3f86f4b2cabf]] brothers Cris and Curt Kirkwood. They skip Smells Like Teen Spirit and close with Lead Belly's Where Did You Sleep Last Night.

years.h: Kurt Cobain found dead at his Seattle home, age 27
years.p: An electrician found Kurt Cobain's body in the room above his garage. The King County medical examiner ruled it suicide by a self-inflicted shotgun wound, about three days earlier.
years.xp:
Nirvana played what turned out to be their last show on March 1 at Terminal Eins in Munich, and the rest of the European tour was postponed after Cobain was diagnosed with bronchitis and laryngitis. On March 4 he was found unconscious after an overdose in a Rome hotel; Courtney Love later said it was a suicide attempt.

Late in March he entered a rehab center in Los Angeles for heroin addiction and left after less than a week, and on April 6 the band withdrew from Lollapalooza. On April 10 about 7,000 people gathered at Seattle Center for a public vigil, where a recording of Courtney Love reading from his note was played.

years.h: MTV Unplugged in New York debuts at No. 1
years.p: Released seven months after Kurt Cobain's death, the Sony Music Studios set tops the Billboard 200 and wins the Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album in 1996.
play: Where Did You Sleep Last Night

eras.title: A band LLC and one song in a vault
eras.text: The surviving members went separate ways, Dave Grohl to Foo Fighters and Krist Novoselic to politics and smaller bands. The catalog they left became the subject of a long fight with Courtney Love.

years.h: Courtney Love's lawsuit ends; You Know You're Right comes out
years.p: Courtney Love had blocked a planned box set in 2001, suing Krist Novoselic and Dave Grohl over Nirvana LLC. The 2002 settlement freed the last studio song, You Know You're Right, for a best-of called Nirvana.
years.xp: The box set followed in November 2004 as With the Lights Out.

eras.title: Surviving members, borrowed singers
eras.text: For thirty years the surviving members refused to tour as Nirvana, but kept turning up for one-off sets with guest singers. Meanwhile the baby from the Nevermind cover took them to court.

years.h: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, first year eligible
years.p: At Barclays Center in Brooklyn, Nirvana are inducted with [[Joan Jett|f376828a-b438-4fda-bb2e-dcd5fbe81f83]], [[Kim Gordon|19301485-ac9c-4dad-885b-cd8e8c8b4184]], [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]] and Lorde singing in Kurt Cobain's place.
years.xp: After the ceremony the surviving members played a late club show at Saint Vitus in Brooklyn with a rotating cast of guests, including [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]].

years.h: FireAid: Nirvana's surviving members play for L.A. fire relief
years.p: Dave Grohl, Krist Novoselic and Pat Smear reunite at the FireAid benefit with guest singers. Two weeks later, on February 14, they play Smells Like Teen Spirit with Post Malone on SNL's 50th anniversary show.

years.h: Nevermind baby Spencer Elden's lawsuit dismissed again
years.p: Spencer Elden sued in 2021 claiming the Nevermind cover was child pornography. A judge granted Nirvana summary judgment in 2025, and Elden appealed again.
years.xp: The suit was first dismissed in 2022, revived by the Ninth Circuit in December 2023, then dismissed on summary judgment. Elden filed a new appeal in October 2025.
